Search Committee
Department of Biology
Pinemoor University
Athens, GA
Dear Members of the Search Committee,
I'm applying for the Assistant Professor of Forest Ecology position in your Department of Biology. I'm a
postdoctoral researcher at Cottonhollow University, where I study how forests recover after severe
wildfire, and I'd like to build a field program in the Southeast, where fire plays a very different role.
My research asks which plants and animals help a burned forest come back, and how fast. My dissertation
showed that birds carry seeds much farther into burned areas than current models assume. My postdoc
work follows what happens next, on 48 plots across two fire scars. Both projects mix field data with
statistical models, and both have produced data sets other labs now use.
I enjoy teaching most when students collect their own data. As instructor of record for Field Methods in
Ecology, I rebuilt the course around two weekend field trips and a final project each student designed. In
my lab, undergraduates own a small question from the start; two of them presented their own posters this
year.
At Pinemoor I'd start with longleaf pine sites, where frequent fire is the norm rather than the exception,
and I'd look for ways to work with your land management partners. Thank you for considering my
application. My research and teaching statements are attached.
Sincerely,
Nadia Petrakis
